name: Tie a bowline without looking
blurb: The king of knots: a fixed loop that will not slip, will not jam, and unties easily after loading. Being able to tie it behind your back, in the dark, is a genuinely practical goal.
steps: Learn it in the open with the rabbit story: the rabbit comes up the hole, round the tree and back down the hole.
Tie it fifty times looking, checking each time that the loose end finishes inside the loop, not outside.
Tie it with your eyes closed, feeling for the twist that forms the hole.
Learn the one-handed version, which is the one you would actually use if you were holding on with the other hand.
Tie it behind your back, then around your own waist, then in the dark.
Learn to spot a cowboy bowline — the mirrored, weaker version — by feel.
tips: Under a cyclic load a bowline can shake loose. Add a stopper knot in the tail if it matters.
Check the tail is inside the loop, every single time. This is the one error that makes it fail.
proof: You tie a correct bowline around your own waist, in the dark, in under ten seconds.
